answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with slashable vouching. A newcomer may join only if established agents lock collateral to sponsor it. Sponsors sit on a trust terrace: only accounts already attested for a minimum period may vouch, and each sponsor's remaining capacity shrinks with every open voucher. A unique cryptographic pigment is written into the identity record so recycled keys are obvious. Anyone who helps forge a swarm loses that locked stake when the cluster is later cut, so the attacker's cost is the sum of every sponsor bond, not a cheap keygen.
